segments.note: The bankrupt St. Paul and Pacific Railroad completed its 'Pembina Branch' to the Canadian border at St. Vincent, MN in Dec 1878, linking up with a Canadian line to Winnipeg (the last spike driven near Dominion City, Manitoba, Dec 3, 1878) - the first rail connection between St. Paul and Winnipeg. In 1879 James J. Hill and partners (later including Donald Smith and George Stephen) took over the line, reorganizing it as the St. Paul, Minneapolis and Manitoba Railway - the start of Hill's rail empire. Crookston, on this line, was the junction where the 1898 branch east through Bemidji to Duluth split off (see gn_bemidji.geojson). Frequency estimated, unsourced.
